skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=true, severity=major. The quotes are real. FY2025 10-K index p.20 (printed 19) says the Biktarvy negotiated price will be 'substantially lower' and 'may also lead to increased rebates we owe Medicaid agencies and reduced ceiling prices charged to 340B covered entities'. But the spillover warning is NOT new. The FY2024 10-K index p.20 (printed 19), in the same IRA bullet, already says negotiation 'could also affect the Medicaid rebate obligations and the ceiling prices charged to covered entities under Section 340B ... if such prices are lower than the Medicaid Best Price'. What changed is the Biktarvy selection (public Jan 2026) and the word 'substantially'. The math also fails. 7,187 = Part D gross spend 2025 ($4,011M) + Medicaid reimbursed 2024 ($3,176M) (medicare_market.csv biktarvy rows). That adds two different years, and both are pre-rebate payer spend (Part D spend includes pharmacy margin), so dividing by Gilead's U.S. NET Biktarvy sales ($11,467M, 10-K FY2025 index p.40) gives 62.7%, which is not a share of anything. Medicaid net is far below reimbursed amount after statutory and CPI rebates. The '$1,147M per 10%' illustration applies a 10% cut to ALL U.S. Biktarvy sales, but the MFP applies only to Medicare, and the filing does not size the Medicaid/340B spillover. The arithmetic checks (1,147/29,443 = 3.9%), but the scenario is unanchored and starts in 2028. Correction: Narrow to: the FY2025 10-K now applies the existing IRA spillover warning to a named drug (Biktarvy, 48.7% of revenue) and says the Medicare price will be 'substantially lower' starting 2028. The 340B wording got stronger ('pervasive violations', index p.21). No dollar sizing is supportable from the filing. Do not present 62.7% as a government-channel share.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=true, severity=fatal. Both lenses kill it. I re-checked the FY2024 10-K (index p.20): the 'could also affect the Medicaid rebate obligations and the ceiling prices charged to covered entities under Section 340B' sentence is there, as both of us found in round 1. The obviousness skeptic adds that the same sentence ran in the 10-Qs from 2024Q3 and that 340B mix came up on calls. On my lens, the 62.7% share mixes years and mixes gross with net. With no 'new' disclosure left to stand on, severity goes up to fatal. Correction: At most a language-drift footnote: the 340B wording hardened to 'pervasive violations'. No number. Conceded: Obviousness is right that the spillover was already in the FY2024 10-K and the 10-Qs. I raise the severity from major to fatal. Held: My math objection stands on its own: 7,187/11,467 adds 2025 Part D gross spend to 2024 Medicaid reimbursed amounts and divides by net sales. Narrowed: Only the 340B wording drift is left, and it is unquantified.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=true, severity=fatal. The Biktarvy IRA selection is a public January 2026 headline and sits inside the case's starter thread (how long the HIV franchise can hold). The claimed 'new' part, spillover into Medicaid rebates and 340B ceiling prices, is not new. The FY2024 10-K already said Medicare negotiation 'could also affect the Medicaid rebate obligations and the ceiling prices charged to covered entities under Section 340B ... if such prices are lower than the Medicaid Best Price' (GILD:10k_FY2024.md p.20, index page 20). The same sentence appears in the 10-Qs from 2024Q3 onward (GILD:companies/GILD/10q_2024Q3.md p.40). The FY2025 10-K (p.20) only changes 'could' to 'may also lead to' once Biktarvy was named. The 340B shift from 'limits the prices we may charge' (GILD:10k_FY2024.md p.21) to 'pervasive violations' (GILD:10k_FY2025.md p.21) is real wording drift, but analysts asked about it directly on calls: Alex Hammond (Wolfe) asked about 340B channel mix and Johanna Mercier replied that 340B had grown 'in every quarter from 2024 into 2025' and named duplicate discounts (GILD:companies/GILD/transcripts/2025Q1_transcript.md p.18, grade C). Mercier also said in 2024Q3 that 340B growth 'can impact the Medicaid patient population' (2024Q3_transcript p.18, grade C). Any IRA model built on Medicaid best price already includes the spillover by statute. Correction: At most a narrow language-drift note: the FY2025 10-K hardens the 340B wording to 'pervasive violations' and 'out of scope percentage of sales.' It does not support a claim that Gilead newly disclosed IRA spillover.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=true, severity=fatal. The two lenses agree. The materiality skeptic independently found the same FY2024 10-K p.20 sentence on Medicaid rebates and 340B ceiling prices that I used. They also showed that the reader's 62.7% government-channel share adds Part D gross spend for 2025 to Medicaid reimbursements for 2024 and divides by net sales. I re-read GILD:10k_FY2024.md p.20 and GILD:10k_FY2025.md pp.20-21, and nothing new there changes the verdict. Correction: Keep at most one supporting line: the FY2025 10-K hardens the 340B wording to 'pervasive violations'. Give no dollar sizing. Conceded: Their math critique is right, and I had not tested it. The 62.7% mixes years and mixes gross with net, and the 10% price cut is applied to all U.S. sales when the negotiated price covers Medicare only. Held: Refuted as obvious. The spillover language dates to the FY2024 10-K, and the Biktarvy selection was a January 2026 headline. Narrowed: Nothing to narrow. The two lenses now agree.

verdict_reason: Both skeptics found the Medicaid-rebate and 340B ceiling-price spillover sentence already in the FY2024 10-K (GILD:10k_FY2024.md index p.20), so the 'new disclosure' premise fails. Obviousness adds that the same sentence ran in the 10-Qs from 2024Q3 (GILD:companies/GILD/10q_2024Q3.md p.40) and that the Biktarvy selection was a January 2026 headline. skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=false, severity=major. The core numbers hold. FY2025 10-K index p.41 shows GTN $19,953M vs $17,776M (+12%) and 41% vs 38% of gross, and the 10-K itself states '250 bps'. Net product sales were 28,915 vs 28,610 (index p.40). Gross 48,868 vs 46,386 = +5.35%. Rate 40.83% vs 38.32%. The derived claims are wrong in three ways. (a) 'Stopped giving the rebate-vs-other split' is overstated. The FY2025 footnote on index p.41 still gives rebates and chargebacks of $17.5B vs $15.5B, so other deductions are about $2.45B vs $2.28B, about 35.8%/5.0% vs 33.4%/4.9% of gross. Only the printed percentages were dropped. (b) '$1,227M of net revenue lost' treats 2025 gross at the 2024 GTN rate as attainable net. Much of the gross growth is list inflation: Biktarvy WAC +5.9% on 2025-01-01 (wac_increases.csv rows 544-546) against gross +5.35%. A list increase that is rebated away raises GTN dollars and the GTN rate without ever having been net revenue. Mix also moves the rate: Veklury, a hospital product, fell $888M, and Descovy rose $645M (index p.40). (c) The '$327M unexplained' compares a company-wide realized residual to a GUIDANCE assumption scoped to HIV. The ~$900M is 'expected headwind ... in 2025' on the JPM 2026 slide p.5 tied to HIV revenue, and 'No change to other assumptions including ~$900M Medicare Part D Redesign impact' on the 2025Q3 slides p.25. On the grade-A 2025Q3 call p.12, the $900M is the analyst's (Mohit Bansal) number, and the CCO (Johanna Mercier) says only that 'those assumptions have not changed'. The 10-K says Part D also hit Liver Disease (index p.41). The residual is therefore not a finding. Correction: Keep: the GTN rate rose about 250 bps to 41% while gross grew about 5.3% and net grew 1.1%, and the 10-K attributes it primarily to Part D redesign. Drop the '$1.2B lost' and '$327M unexplained' framing. If a dollar figure is wanted, say that 100 bps of GTN on about $48.9B gross equals about $489M of net sales (1.7% of revenue), as a sensitivity. Replace 'stopped giving the split' with 'stopped printing the percentages; rebates and chargebacks are still given in dollars ($17.5B vs $15.5B)'.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=true, severity=fatal. I verified the obviousness skeptic's sources. The 2025Q4 earnings slides p.25 say 'Excluding an estimated $1.1 billion in Part D Redesign headwinds, total product sales +5%'. The 2024Q4 call p.10 (grade C, CFO Andrew Dickinson) says 'approximately $1.1 billion, including $900 million in HIV'. Measured against the company-wide figure, the reader's residual is 1,227 - 1,100 = about $127M, or 0.4% of revenue. That is below the materiality threshold even before my round 1 objection. That objection still applies: the rate-at-2024 counterfactual counts list-price inflation that was never net revenue (Biktarvy WAC +5.9% against gross +5.35%), plus mix (Veklury -$888M), so the true unexplained amount is plausibly about zero. The 250 bps headline is printed in the 10-K's own GTN table, and the dollar rebate split is still disclosed. Correction: Usable only as context: GTN +250 bps, about 90% of it the $1.1B Part D headwind management sized. No finding. Conceded: In round 1 I held c03 in narrowed form. I now concede it. Management gave a company-wide $1.1B figure that I did not find, which shrinks the residual to an immaterial $127M, and the 250 bps rate rise is printed in the 10-K itself. Held: The '$1.2B lost net revenue' framing is wrong arithmetic regardless of which Part D figure is used, because list inflation and mix both inflate the counterfactual. Narrowed: From 'held, narrowed' to refuted: nothing material and unsaid remains.
